In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

Tafsir of Surah As-Sajdah

It is Makkan, except for three verses which were revealed concerning ʿAlī, may Allah be pleased with him, which we will mention.

Jābir has narrated that the Prophet (ﷺ) would not sleep each night until he had recited "Alif Lām Mīm, the revelation" (As-Sajdah) and "Blessed is He in whose hand is the dominion" (Al-Mulk).

It is also established that the Prophet (ﷺ) used to recite Surah As-Sajdah and Surah "Hal Atā" in the Fajr prayer on Friday.

As for the words of the Most High: ﴿Alif, Lām, Mīm. The revelation of the Book, wherein there is no doubt, is from the Lord of the worlds﴾, meaning: there is no doubt in it. Ar-rayb (doubt) is ash-shakk (suspicion, uncertainty), and we have explained it before.

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

Tafsir of Surah As-Sajdah

It is Makkan, except for three verses which were revealed concerning ʿAlī, may Allah be pleased with him, which we will mention.

Jābir has narrated that the Prophet (ﷺ) would not sleep each night until he had recited "Alif Lām Mīm, the revelation" (As-Sajdah) and "Blessed is He in whose hand is the dominion" (Al-Mulk).

It is also established that the Prophet (ﷺ) used to recite Surah As-Sajdah and Surah "Hal Atā" in the Fajr prayer on Friday.

As for the words of the Most High: ﴿Alif, Lām, Mīm. The revelation of the Book, wherein there is no doubt, is from the Lord of the worlds﴾, meaning: there is no doubt in it. Ar-rayb (doubt) is ash-shakk (suspicion, uncertainty), and we have explained it before.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 32, verse 3:

His saying: ﴿Or do they say, "He has invented it"?﴾ Its meaning is: "Rather, they say, 'He has invented it.'" The poet said, using "am" (or) with the meaning of "bal" (rather):

(Your eye has deceived you, or did you see in Wasit the darkness of night over the Rabab mountains?)

Its meaning is: "Rather, you saw."

And His saying: ﴿Rather, it is the truth from your Lord, that you may warn a people to whom no warner has come before you﴾

Here "ma" carries the meaning of negation, and its meaning is: that you may warn a people whose forefathers, as well as they themselves, did not witness a prophet before you. If it is said: if they did not witness a prophet and were not warned, how can they be held accountable to the Fire for abandoning faith? The answer: it was incumbent on them to believe in God through the sending of the messengers who came before, and they had heard of that.

Some of them said: Isma'il was a prophet to the Arabs, and they abandoned his religion. It is also said that they abandoned the religion of Ibrahim, peace be upon him.

And His saying: ﴿so that they may be guided﴾ means: that they may be rightly guided.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 32, verse 4:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿It is Allah who created the heavens and the earth and whatever is between them in six days﴾. This has already been explained. It is reported from al-Hasan that he said: it is one day of the days of this world. If someone says: when Allah created the heavens and the earth, there was no day or night, so how does this statement hold together? The answer: its meaning is: in the measure of six days of the days of this world.

And His saying: ﴿Then He established Himself above the Throne﴿. This has already been explained.

And His saying: ﴿You have no guardian or intercessor besides Him. Will you not then take heed?﴾ Its meaning: will you not then be admonished?

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 32, verse 5:

The words of the Exalted: ﴿He arranges the affair from the heaven to the earth﴾, meaning: He judges and decides the affair from the heaven to the earth.

And His saying: ﴿Then it ascends to Him﴾. Regarding "then" (thumma) there are two opinions. The first: then the angel ascends to Him after descending with the command. The second opinion: then it ascends to Him, meaning the affair ascends to Him. The meaning of the affair ascending to Him is that the whole affair returns to Him and the affairs of all creation are withdrawn.

And His saying: ﴿in a Day whose measure is a thousand years of what you count﴾. This verse is considered problematic, and the problem is that God the Exalted said in another verse: ﴿in a Day whose measure is fifty thousand years﴾. Mujahid said: ﴿in a Day whose measure is a thousand years﴾ means that the distance from the heaven to the earth, when the angel descends, is five hundred years, and when he ascends, five hundred years, so it becomes a thousand years.

As for His saying: ﴿fifty thousand years﴾, it is from the floor of the earth to the Throne. Some of them said: fifty thousand years and a thousand years are all on the Day of Resurrection, so the Day of Resurrection is a thousand years for some and fifty thousand years for others, and the day is one.

In some reports: "Indeed God the Exalted shortens it for the believer until it is as the time between two prayers" (ﷺ).

Some of them said: some angels ascend in the measure of a thousand years, and some angels ascend in the measure of fifty thousand years. And God knows best.

That is (ﷺ)... no, correcting myself: this is the Qur'anic verse 32:6 commentary, so I translate as follows.

On His saying, the Exalted: ﴿That is the Knower of the unseen and the witnessed﴾, meaning: what is absent from the servants and what is not absent from them. It is also said: the unseen is what is in the Hereafter, and the witnessed is what is in this world.

And His saying: ﴿the Mighty, the Merciful﴾, meaning: the Invincible in His dominion, the Merciful to His creation.

The words of the Exalted: ﴿He who perfected everything He created﴾. It is also read "khalqahu" with a fatha on the lam. Whoever reads "khalqahu" (as a verb, "khalaqa") means: He perfected the creation of everything. Whoever reads "khalqahu" (as a noun, "khalq") means: the goodness of everything He created.

Ibn ʿAbbas said: ﴿He perfected everything He created﴾ means: He made it firm and well-ordered (atqana wa-ahkama).

It was also said: As for the buttock of the monkey, it is not beautiful, but it is well-made (muhkam). It was also said: He created the beasts in the form of beasts, and the human beings in the form of human beings. He did not create human beings in the form of beasts, nor beasts in the form of human beings. So every living creature is complete and good in its creation. This is the meaning of the saying of the earlier wise men: "Every living creature is complete in its deficiency"; that is, if it is compared with something else it is found deficient, yet in itself and in its equipment it is complete. Some of them mentioned, regarding the meaning of the verse: the length of the leg of the beast and the length of the neck of the bird, so that each of them may reach its sustenance.

And the words of Allah: ﴿And He began the creation of man from clay﴾, meaning: Adam and his offspring.

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Then He made his offspring from an extract of a liquid, despised.﴾ We have already explained the meaning of "sulalah" (extract). As for His words ﴿from a liquid, despised﴾, it means: weak.

God's words, "Then He proportioned him and breathed into him of His spirit" have already been discussed.

His words, "And He made for you hearing, sight, and hearts," mean: the hearings, the sights, and the hearts.

His words, "Little is it that you give thanks," mean: little is it that you give thanks.

"The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿And they say, 'When we have been lost in the earth, shall we indeed be in a new creation?'﴾ That is: when we have perished in the earth. It is said: 'The milk was lost (ḍalla) in the water,' meaning it perished. It is also said: 'We have decayed and become dust.' And it is recited in the irregular (shādhdh) reading as 'ṣalalnā' with an unpointed ṣād, meaning: we have changed, as one says, 'the meat became ṣalla' when it stinks.

And His words: ﴿Shall we indeed be in a new creation?﴾ That is: shall we return alive after we have died. They said this by way of denial and rejection.

And His words: ﴿Nay, they are disbelievers in the meeting with their Lord﴾ That is: they are deniers of the Resurrection after death."

**Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 32, verse 11:**

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Say: The angel of death who has been entrusted with you will take you back﴾. The angel of death is ʿAzrāʾīl. It has been said: He takes you back Himself. It is also said: He takes you back through his assistants. In some reports it is related that the angel of death stands on a ladder (miʿrāj) between heaven and earth, and his assistants draw out the human soul; when it reaches the hollow of the throat, the angel of death seizes it. It is also related that the world, in the sight of the angel of death, is like a basin between a man's two feet.

From Anas, may Allah be pleased with him, that he said: Jibrīl met the angel of death at the sea of Fārs, and said: "O angel of death, how do you seize the souls of people when the plague (wabāʾ) occurs, so that ten thousand die on this side and ten thousand on that side?" He said: "The earth is folded up between my eyes, and I snatch them up, snatching them."

Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad related from his father: The Prophet (ﷺ) entered upon a man of the Anṣār visiting him, and he saw the angel of death at his head. So he said to him: "Be gentle with this man, one of my companions." He said: "Be at ease and cool of eye, for I am gentle with every believer." Then he said: "O Muḥammad, by Him in whose hand is my soul, if I wished to seize the soul of a gnat I would not be able to do so until Allah commands its seizing. I scan the faces of people every day five times." This report is gharīb (rare).

In some of the Musnads, through the narration of Anas, the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Illnesses and pains are the messengers of death. When the angel of death seizes the soul of a servant, and they cry out over him, he says: 'What are you crying out about? By Allah, I have not diminished his provision, nor brought forward his term, nor wronged any of you. Rather, Allah called him and he answered. So let every man weep for himself. And I will return to you again and again, until I leave none of you.'" This report is also among the gharīb reports.

As for tawaffī, it means the completion of the number, and its meaning is that He seizes their souls until no one remains of the number whose death has been decreed. The poet said:

(Indeed, the sons of al-Adram are not of any single group... nor does Quraysh complete their number.)

That is: Quraysh does not complete their number.

His saying: ﴿Then to your Lord you will be returned﴾, meaning: you will go.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 32, verse 12:

The words of the Most High: ﴿And if only you could see when the criminals will hang their heads before their Lord﴾. Its meaning: And if only you could see the criminals hanging their heads, out of extreme regret and intense dread. In the verse there is an ellipsis (hadhf), and the omitted part is: "Had you seen the criminals hanging their heads before their Lord, you would have seen something from which one takes warning."

And His words: ﴿Our Lord, we have seen and heard﴾, meaning: saying, "Our Lord, we have seen and heard," that is: we have seen the truth of Your threat and heard from You the confirmation of Your messengers. Qatadah said: "They saw when sight no longer benefited them, and they heard when hearing no longer benefited them." It is also said: "We have seen our sins, and we have heard what was said about us."

And His words: ﴿So return us, that we may do righteous deeds﴾, meaning: send us back so that we may do righteous deeds.

And His words: ﴿Indeed, we are now certain﴾, meaning: we now affirm the Resurrection.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 32, verse 13:

His statement, exalted is He: ﴿And if We had willed, We would have given every soul its guidance﴾, meaning: its guidance. Its meaning: if We had willed, We would have caused them to enter into faith.

And His statement: ﴿But the word from Me has come into effect﴾, meaning: the word from Me has become obligatory. It is also said: the word from Me has preceded. The poet said:

(So if there is reproach, then welcome and greetings... and the reproach has become binding upon you with us, and it was said)

And His statement: ﴿I will surely fill Hell with jinn and men, all together﴾.

And His statement: ﴿the jinn﴾ are the jinn, and al-Jann is the father of the jinn, just as Adam is the father of (mankind).

Khārijah transmitted a report to the Prophet (ﷺ) that he was asked whether believing jinn enter Paradise. He said: "Yes." It was said: "Do they partake of its bounties?" He said: "Allah inspires them with His glorification and His remembrance, and they receive from Him what the children of Adam receive of the bounties of Paradise." Al-Naqqash related this in his tafsir.

It is also established from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "Paradise and Hell disputed. The Fire said: 'I have been favoured with the tyrants and the arrogant.' Paradise said: 'What is the matter with me that the weak and the lowly of people enter me?'" In another narration: "the weak of people and their poor," and this is the more well-known. Then Allah, exalted is He, said to Paradise: "You are My mercy; I show mercy through you to whomever I will." And He said to the Fire: "You are My punishment; I punish through you whomever I will. And each of you will have its fill."

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 32, verse 14:

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿So taste [the punishment] for your forgetting the meeting of this your Day﴾, meaning: for what you abandoned of believing in the meeting of this your Day.

And His saying: ﴿Indeed, We have forgotten you﴾, meaning: We have abandoned you from good and mercy. It was also said: We have abandoned you in the punishment.

And His saying: ﴿And taste the punishment of eternity for what you used to do﴾, meaning: the lasting punishment as a recompense for your deeds. And it is related from Qatadah that he said, concerning His saying: ﴿But the word from Me is truly fulfilled: I will surely fill Hell with jinn and mankind all together﴾, meaning: because of their sins. Al-Azhari (al-Azhari) said: "And it is as he said."

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 32, verse 15:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Only those believe in Our signs who, when they are reminded of them, fall down prostrate and glorify the praise of their Lord, and they are not arrogant.﴾ That is, when they are called to the five prayers, they respond to them. This was related by Abu Mu'adh al-Nahwi, and it is said: when they are admonished with the signs of God, they take heed.

His saying: ﴿fall down prostrate﴾ means they fell down in prostration. Al-kharur (falling down) in the language means collapsing. It is related from Hakim ibn Hizam that he said: "I pledged allegiance to the Messenger of God that I would not fall (down) except standing," meaning: I will not die except while firm upon Islam. His saying: ﴿and glorify the praise of their Lord﴾ means they pray by the command of their Lord.

It is also said: they glorify [God] and praise Him.

His saying: ﴿and they are not arrogant﴾ means they are not proud. It is said: whoever prostrates to God has cast off pride from his head. And in some reports: whoever prostrates to God one prostration, God raises him thereby one degree.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 32, verse 16:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Their sides forsake their beds﴾, meaning: they rise up and lift themselves away. Its meaning is that they leave their beds and stand up to prayer. Hassan ibn Thabit said:

(He spends the night holding his side away from his bed, when the beds weigh heavy upon the polytheists.)

There is disagreement concerning this verse. It is narrated from ʿAtaʾ that he said: "They would not sleep until they had prayed the ʿAtamah (the night prayer after twilight), so God sent down this verse."

It is narrated from al-Hasan and Qatadah that they both said: it refers to prayer between Maghrib and ʿIshaʾ.

Al-Dahhak said: when they awoke, they remembered God and glorified Him.

It is narrated from Abu al-Darda', Abu Dharr and ʿUbadah ibn al-Samit, may God be pleased with them, that they said: it refers to the late night prayer (ʿIshaʾ) and the Fajr prayer in congregation.

The most well-known of these opinions is that what is meant by it is the night prayer (ṣalat al-layl, the voluntary prayer during the night), as said by Mujahid, Malik, al-Awzaʿi and a group of others.

It is narrated from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "Keep to the night prayer, for it is the habit of the righteous before you."

It has also been established from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said concerning ʿAbdullah ibn ʿUmar: "What an excellent man ʿAbdullah is, if only he prayed at night." After that, ʿAbdullah did not abandon the night prayer until God took him.

In the hadith of Muʿadh ibn Jabal, the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Fasting is a shield, charity extinguishes sin, and prayer in the middle of the night." Then he recited the saying of God, may He be exalted: (Their sides forsake their beds).

His saying: ﴿calling upon their Lord in fear and hope﴾, meaning: in fear of the Fire and in hope of Paradise.

His saying: ﴿and from what We have provided for them they spend﴾. It is said that what is meant by it is the obligatory zakah, and it is said: charity and voluntary giving.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 32, verse 17:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿So no soul knows what is hidden for them of comfort for the eyes﴾. It was also read as "qurrat a'yun" (qurrat a'yun, the plural form of the reading).

It is firmly established from the Prophet (ﷺ), by the transmission of Abu al-Zinad, from al-A'raj, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Allah, may He be exalted, says: I have prepared for My righteous servants what no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and no human heart has conceived. So recite, if you wish, His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿So no soul knows what is hidden for them of comfort for the eyes﴾."

The Shaykh, the Imam, said: This hadith was related to us by Abu 'Ali al-Shafi'i, who said: Abu al-Hasan ibn [Firas] related to us, who said: Abu Muhammad 'Abd Allah ibn 'Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Muqri' related to us, who said: My grandfather Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Yazid al-Muqri' related to us, who said: Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah related to us, from Abu al-Zinad... the report.

As for His saying, ﴿of comfort for the eyes﴾, it means: that by which their eyes are gladdened. Al-Naqqash related in his exegesis, from Musa ibn Yasar, who said: The believer remains in Paradise with his wife for a time, then another (wife) looks down upon him, and says to him: "Has the time not come for us to have a turn with you?" He says to her: "Who are you?" She says: "I am one of those about whom Allah, may He be exalted, said: ﴿So no soul knows what is hidden for them of comfort for the eyes﴾." So he goes over to her and remains with her for a time. Then another looks down upon him and says what the first said. He says to her: "Who are you?" She says: "I am one of those about whom Allah, may He be exalted, said: ﴿And with Us is more﴾."

And from Ibn Sirin, he said: "What is hidden for them of comfort for the eyes" is looking upon Allah, may He be exalted. (And from some of them) he said: They concealed their deeds, so Allah concealed their reward.

Al-Hasan al-Basri said: The concealed (deed) is repaid with the concealed (reward), and the open (deed) with the open (reward).

As for His saying, ﴿as a reward for what they used to do﴾, its meaning is apparent.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 32, verse 18:

The words of the Exalted: ﴿Is then one who is a believer like one who is a defiant sinner?﴾ Most of the exegetes (mufassirun) say that the verse was revealed concerning ʿAli ibn Abi Talib and al-Walid ibn ʿUqba ibn Abi Muʿayt. Some of them mention ʿUqba instead, but the more correct view is the first. Al-Walid said: "I am sharper of spear than you, more eloquent of tongue than you, and fuller for the battalion than you." ʿAli said to him: "Be silent, for you are only a fasiq (defiant sinner)." So God the Exalted revealed this verse. We have already explained that three verses of this surah were revealed in Medina, and they are from this verse to the end of the three. The Mu'tazilites (Ahl al-I'tizal) used this verse to argue for the doctrine of the intermediate position (al-manzila bayn al-manzilatayn), and that the fasiq cannot be a believer. The evidence against them is clear. As for the fasiq here, it means the disbeliever (kafir). Some say that He called him fasiq in agreement with the statement of ʿAli, may God be pleased with him. It was also said: the verse is general in its application.

The words of the Exalted: ﴿They are not equal﴾ meaning: they are not equal in this world or in the Hereafter.

Almighty Allah says: ﴿As for those who believed and did righteous deeds, they will have the Gardens of Refuge as a lodging, for what they used to do.﴾ That is, a reward (ʿaṭāʾ) for what they used to do. The Gardens of Refuge (Jannāt al-Maʾwā) are the gardens to which the believers resort.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 32, verse 20:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿But as for those who defiantly disobeyed, their refuge is the Fire﴾. That is, they [take refuge, ya'wūn] toward the Fire, and "ya'wūn" means they turn back.

And His saying: ﴿Every time they wish to get out of it, they will be returned into it﴾. In some of the exegetical reports: indeed, Hell has a shore like the shore of the sea, so the disbelievers go out onto it, and then venomous snakes, having fangs like palm trees, are sent against them, so they return to the Fire and seek refuge in it.

And His saying: ﴿And it will be said to them, "Taste the punishment of the Fire which you used to deny."﴾ The report we have mentioned was related by Abu al-Husayn Ibn Faris in his tafsir.

"The Word of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿And We will surely make them taste of the lesser punishment﴾. Ibn Mas'ud said: It is the hunger that afflicted the disbelievers, to the point that they ate carrion and dead animals, and that was due to the years of drought the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) invoked against them. And from Ibn 'Abbas, he said: It is the killing at Badr. And from a group of the Successors (tabi'un) that they said: It is calamities. And from some of them: It is the prescribed punishments (hudud). And from Ja'far ibn Muhammad: The lesser punishment is the high price of goods, and the greater punishment is the emergence of al-Mahdi with the sword. And according to the views of those we have mentioned before, the greater punishment is the Day of Resurrection, and we seek refuge with Allah from it.

And His Word: ﴿Besides the greater punishment﴾, i.e., apart from the greater punishment.

And His Word: ﴿So that they may return﴾, i.e., that they may return from disbelief."

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 32, verse 22:

The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿And who is more unjust than one who is reminded of the verses of his Lord﴾ meaning: who is admonished by the verses of his Lord, and the verses of his Lord are the Qur'an.

And His words: ﴿Then turns away from them. Indeed, We will take vengeance upon the criminals﴾. Mu'adh narrated that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Whoever does three things is a criminal (mujrim): whoever ties a banner (liwa') for something other than what is right is a criminal, whoever walks with an oppressor to support him is a criminal, and whoever disobeys his parents is a criminal." Then he recited the words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, We will take vengeance upon the criminals﴾.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 32, verse 23:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And We certainly gave Musa the Book﴾, i.e., the Torah (al-Tawrah).

And His saying: ﴿So do not be in doubt about meeting him﴾, i.e., be not in doubt concerning his meeting. Regarding its meaning there are several opinions. The first: what Abu Salih narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, that its meaning is: "So do not be in doubt about your meeting Musa," and he had met him on the night of the Isra'. And in a report it is related that the Prophet said: "I saw Musa, a man of medium height with curly hair, as if he were one of the men of Shanu'ah, and I saw 'Isa, a man of medium build, reddish, with straight hair..." And the report is long. The second opinion: ﴿So do not be in doubt about his meeting﴾, i.e., about Musa's meeting the Book, and Musa's meeting the Book means receiving it with acceptance; this was mentioned by al-Zajjaj and others. The third opinion: ﴿So do not be in doubt about the meeting of Musa with his Lord﴾, related by al-Naqqash. There is a fourth opinion regarding the verse: that its meaning is according to inversion and postposition, as if He had said: "And We certainly gave Musa the Book, and made it a guidance for the Children of Israel."

And His saying: ﴿So do not be in doubt about his meeting﴾ refers back to what preceded in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And We will surely make them taste the lesser punishment, besides the greater punishment﴾, and its meaning is: "So do not be in doubt about the meeting of the Day of Punishment," and Allah knows best. ﴿And We made it a guidance for the Children of Israel﴾. It is said: it refers back to Musa, and it is said: it refers back to the Book.

And His saying: ﴿And We made from among them leaders﴾, i.e., guides toward good. Some of them said: they are the prophets. Some of them said: they are the followers of the prophets.

And His saying: ﴿guiding by Our command when they were patient﴾, i.e., guiding by Our revelation when they were patient. It was recited "lamma sabaru" (when they were patient), i.e., patient against sins. And it was said: patient against the desires of this world.

And His saying: ﴿and they were certain of Our signs﴾, i.e., they affirmed them as true.

The saying of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, your Lord will judge between them on the Day of Resurrection﴾, meaning: He will issue the judgment that decides between them.

And His saying: ﴿concerning that wherein they used to differ﴾ is clear in meaning.

The Exalted said: ﴿Has it not become clear to them﴾ meaning: Has Muhammad not made clear to them? It was also said: the Book. It is read as "Has We not made clear to them" (أَو لم نهد لَهُم), meaning: We make clear to them.

And His saying: ﴿how many generations We destroyed before them, in whose dwelling-places they walk﴾ meaning: the people of Makkah walk in their dwelling-places.

And His saying: ﴿Indeed, in that are signs. Will they not listen?﴾ meaning: listening that accepts.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 32, verse 27:

The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿Have they not seen that We drive the water to the barren land﴾, meaning: the dry land that does not produce anything. Ibn 'Abbas said: it is a land in Yemen. Mujahid said: it is in al-Andalus. It is also said: the barren land is that whose crops have been eaten and nothing remains in it.

His words: ﴿so We bring forth thereby crops of which their cattle eat﴾, meaning: from the green herbage and the chaff.

His words: ﴿and themselves﴾, meaning: from wheat, barley and the rest of the staple foods.

His words: ﴿Will they not then see?﴾, the meaning is apparent.

"And they say, 'When is this victory, if you are truthful?'" (Qur'an 32:28). About this verse there are several opinions. The first is that "the victory" (al-fath) is the conquest of Makkah. The second is that it is killing by the sword. The third is that it is the Day of Resurrection. The fourth is that it is God's judgment between the servants.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 32, verse 29:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Say: On the Day of Victory, their faith will not benefit those who disbelieved﴾. He means: the Day of Resurrection. And whoever takes "the Victory" to mean the conquest of Makkah, or the killing by the sword on the Day of Badr, and says: the meaning of His saying ﴿their faith will not benefit those who disbelieved﴾ is: after death.

And His saying ﴿nor will they be reprieved﴾ means: they will not be given respite to repent or to make excuses, whereas they were given respite in the world to repent or to make excuses.

"The word of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿So turn away from them﴾. This verse came before the verse of the sword, and the verse of the sword has abrogated it (naskh). It is also said: turn away from their harm, even if they harm you.

And His word: ﴿And wait, for they too are waiting﴾. That is: wait for their punishment and Our threat concerning them, for they are waiting. Similarly, if it is said: how did He say ﴿they are waiting﴾ for the punishment, when they had not believed in the punishment? The answer: since Allah, the Exalted, had promised them the punishment, and that was certainly going to reach them, He called them "waiting" by way of metaphor (majaz) in speech. It is also said: ﴿for they too are waiting﴾, that is: your death and the calamities of time for you, so that they may be relieved of you."
